title: Let close --allow-legacy-usage excuse recovered interrupted-job records
summary: Job 20261015-131540-2fsa's interrupted producer invocation record has token counts that disagree with its models_used. `athena close --allow-legacy-usage` still refuses it, because the flag's scope excuses only records already committed in the parent commit, and a recovered record is a new file. I read the goal as extending the flag, and only the flag, to records `close` itself recovers from the state directory, for token and cost mismatches. The audience is the maintainer running the close.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria check that the close succeeds and reconciles, and that it is still refused without the flag.
Lifecycle and gate tests are added, and cargo test, clippy and fmt must pass.
The change widens the legacy scope for the whole class of recovered records, not just job 2fsa.
The limit is enforced in the gate scope and covered by a negative test.
Docs and decision text are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: crates/athena-gate/src/reconcile.rs already checks tokens in check_invocation (the requested model's per-model tokens must equal the measured ones) and cost. It has committed_invocation_violations and check_tree_excusing_committed, which excuse only records committed in the parent. crates/athena-gate/src/lib.rs defines Scope::CommitLegacyUsage and applies it at about lines 359-373. crates/athena-core/src/manage.rs close_with resolves the job, calls recover_interrupted for a Dispatched job to build new record files, then calls commit_records_in with the scope. The violations are measured directly on the invocation record. The change adds no record or data file under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not affected.

Job 20261015-131540-2fsa is a separate, abandoned job: its candidate changed no files and its study/explainer work was re-asked as job rvmd and landed (f6f60b4). That work is dropped here. This change does not touch studies/firstmate-work-handling/*, xtask/src/site.rs, or the pinned commit. CHANGELOG.md is touched only for this change's own entry.

The 2fsa invocation record exists only in the state directory, so close adds it as a new file in the closing commit and the legacy scope does not cover it. The user did not answer the earlier question about this, so I keep that assumption.

The gate stays strict for everything else. Only the invocation files that close_with recovers itself are excused, and each is printed. Outcome totals, and any invocation record that is new or altered by any other path, are still refused. This narrows nothing and refuses nothing new, so the replay refusal rate is unchanged: expected 0% of newly refused readings.
question: Is the 2fsa invocation record already committed, or does it exist only in the state directory? I assumed the state directory.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new lifecycle test creates an interrupted job whose state-directory invocation record has measured tokens that disagree with its models_used. `athena close --allow-legacy-usage` succeeds, prints a 'letting a legacy usage record through' line naming the token mismatch, and the closing outcome reconciles. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle`.
The same close without the flag is still refused with 'usage records reconcile', and the error names --allow-legacy-usage. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle`.

A gate test shows that under the legacy scope an invocation record that is new or altered outside close's own recovery still fails reconciliation, and a wrong outcome total is still refused. Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`.
`cargo test` passes, and `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

docs/decisions.md has a new decision, or an amendment to D101, giving the case, the alternatives and the limit of the excuse. CHANGELOG.md and the close row in docs/design/athena-v0.md describe the wider coverage.
The flag's help text and doc comments in crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs and crates/athena-core/src/manage.rs state exactly which records it excuses.

out_of_scope: Changing the study files for firstmate-work-handling, xtask/src/site.rs, or the pinned commit (job 2fsa's allowed scope, dropped)
Modifying or rewriting any existing record, including the 2fsa invocation record
Weakening outcome-total reconciliation or excusing new invocation records outside close's own recovery
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass chance than the reference because the change touches the gate scope and needs several tests and docs.
hard_reason: It changes the close gate's scope, a rule that can refuse work, in the reconciliation gate that judges jobs.
